clue.text: In opposition 8 follow the case

parts.note: to follow someone closely is to shadow them
a cabinet is a case or cupboard for storing things

explanation.surface: Someone in the opposition is told to follow the case through.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition cross-refers to 8 down, FRONTBENCHERS: the opposition's frontbenchers are the team that mirrors the government's ministers in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior opposition politicians who each mirror a minister form this body in British politics.

clue.text: Showing respect of choir in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio programme shows reverence for a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the radio picture but signals rearranging the letters of OF CHOIR IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A title such as Sir or Reverend is a respectful form of address, so the adjective means conveying esteem.

clue.text: Dim woman lacks ego

indicators.note: lacks says something is missing from the woman's name

parts.note: Denise is a woman's name
ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A slow-witted woman has no self-esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim and dense are both informal synonyms for slow-witted or stupid.

clue.text: Regularly swore to love no-good criminal

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word swore

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
NG is a common abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A criminal who swore he loved a worthless crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of SWORE, W and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal can mean morally or legally wrong, as in a wrong or criminal act.

clue.text: A sundial inaccurately showing afternoon in part of Spain

indicators.note: a sundial showing inaccurately suggests its letters are set wrongly

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for afternoon, as in p.m. contexts (ante/after)

explanation.surface: A sundial in southern Spain tells the afternoon hours badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurately' rearranges A SUNDIAL into ANDALUSI, and the afternoon's A is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the large autonomous region of southern Spain containing Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Guerrilla and I with a gun back in the car

indicators.note: in places the reversed weapon inside the car's letters

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a car

indicators.note: back says the words a gun are read from the end

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter boasts of riding with a gun in the back of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives REGULA, which goes 'in' the car; 'Guerrilla' is the definition, not part of a picture of an armed rebel's getaway. RR for Rolls-Royce is a standard crossword car.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular troops are those outside a regular army, such as guerrilla fighters.

clue.text: Boredom of a kind experienced by English nun travelling to Italy

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of nun shift around

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An English nun grows weary on her journey to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' gives the middle three letters; 'of a kind experienced by' links the definition to the scene it describes, a weary journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a kind of tedium.

clue.text: Senior politicians face senior lawyers

parts.note: the face of something is its front
benchers are senior members of the Inns of Court in London

explanation.surface: Leading MPs come up against eminent barristers.
explanation.walkthrough: BENCHERS are the senior barristers and judges who govern London's Inns of Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers and their opposition shadows sit on the front benches of the House of Commons.

clue.text: Officer's mode of transport during 1926 crisis

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer; the 's adds S
a trike, a tricycle, is a mode of transport

explanation.surface: How an army officer got around during a national emergency of 1926.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1926 General Strike was a nine-day stoppage across Britain in support of the coal miners.
explanation.definitionFit: The great British stoppage of May 1926 is known as the General Strike, a nationwide walkout.

clue.text: Argument with transport officer in "Brief Encounter"

parts.note: a run-in is a quarrel or argument
TO stands for transport officer in military usage

explanation.surface: A row with an official in the classic film Brief Encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is a famous 1945 British film set at a railway station; here it simply means meeting someone briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, a short unplanned encounter.

clue.text: Madden monarch who's in endless peril

indicators.note: in places the monarch inside the shortened peril
endless says the word for peril loses its last letter

parts.note: peril means danger
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A king whose life is constantly at risk is driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives DANGE; the 'monarch' goes 'in' it. The surface imagines a king's madness, but 'Madden' is the verb for driving mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden or derange someone is to drive them out of their mind.

clue.text: Foster-sister?

definitions.meaning: to foster is to tend and cherish, as in fostering an idea or a child
a sister is a senior hospital ward ... in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins two definitions into the look of a single family word; in Britain a sister is a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to tend or nurture, and the noun is the hospital role a sister holds.

clue.text: Element added to brown coal to make explosive

parts.note: Ge is the chemical symbol of the element germanium
lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: A chemical is combined with soft coal to make a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a high explosive made from nitroglycerine, used in blasting.

clue.text: Easily disheartened, boy fliers turned back

indicators.note: disheartened says the heart, the middle letter, is removed from boy
turned back says the word for fliers is read in reverse

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers

explanation.surface: A dejected lad's flying aces readily retreated.
explanation.definitionFit: By far means by a wide margin, so easily ahead as in winning easily.

clue.text: City cad supported by mother

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a scoundrel
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A scoundrel in town is propped up by his mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major Dutch port city in South Holland.

clue.text: Jockey displays a growth abnormality

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre into position, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rider shows a strange lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' reads as a rider but is the verb meaning to manoeuvre, rearranging DISPLAYS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysplasia is the medical term for abnormal development or growth of cells or tissue.

clue.text: Pressed Gordon first about reshuffling Balls

indicators.note: first says the rearranged piece comes before the other
reshuffling, as in a cabinet reshuffle, rearranges these letters

parts.note: a is an abbreviation for about, as with approximate dates
Ed Balls was a Labour minister under Gordon Brown

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown pushed his allies around in a cabinet reshuffle involving Ed Balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffling' and 'first' are both needed; the surface recalls Gordon Brown's Labour cabinet, where Ed Balls was a close ally. Reading 'a' for about is a dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dragooned is to be coerced or pressed into doing something.

clue.text: Comic character, wonderful Shakespearean role

parts.note: super means wonderful
Hero is the heroine of Much Ado About Nothing

explanation.surface: A marvellous part in Shakespeare for a funny actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' means a comic book, not a funny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Caped crusaders of comic books are the classic superheroes.

clue.text: CIA involvement with nation which produces tobacco

indicators.note: involvement suggests the letters are entangled and mixed together

explanation.surface: The CIA's dealings with a country that grows tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement with' rearranges CIA and NATION together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the plant genus that includes tobacco and ornamental relatives.

clue.text: Maybe stays in quarantine in Cairo pesthouse?

indicators.note: kept in quarantine means shut up inside, so the answer sits within the words

explanation.surface: People isolated in a plague hospital in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are ropes that brace a ship's mast, so 'Maybe' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays on a sailing ship are ropes, so stays are an example of the general term.

clue.text: Parliamentary duties mostly undertaken by women?

definitions.text: Parliamentary duties mostly undertaken by women?

parts.words: Parliamentary duties mostly undertaken by women
parts.note: read as the work of the House of Commons, then as domestic chores traditionally left to women

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the business of Parliament, the House; the other reading is cleaning the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic chores like cleaning and tidying are traditionally associated with women.

clue.text: One local fellow's cow

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A local chap owns a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is the verb meaning to intimidate, not the farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, which is to rob them of courage.

clue.text: Currency used over in Yemen or Kuwait

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are read upward, backwards
in says the answer lies within the words Yemen or Kuwait

explanation.surface: Money spent in Arabian states.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ENORK sits 'in' YEMEN OR KUWAIT, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency unit of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: One tends to hurry pointlessly

indicators.note: pointlessly means without a compass point, here East

parts.note: to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after others tends to rush about without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer is someone who looks after a sick or elderly person.

clue.text: Literary sergeant's way of dealing with naughty boys?

definitions.meaning: Sergeant Cuff is the detective in Wilkie Collins's novel The Moonstone

definitions.text: way of dealing with naughty boys?
definitions.meaning: slaps or blows to the head, an old punishment

explanation.walkthrough: Sergeant Cuff of The Moonstone (1868) is an early fictional detective; the possessive gives the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Light blows with the hand are an old way of punishing children, and the sergeant's name with possessive matches.

clue.text: Fast-moving drama starts to attract notice

indicators.note: moving means changing position, so the letters of drama shift
starts to asks for the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A gripping play quickly gets attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it is the noun. 'moving' gives RAMAD from the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daytime fasting.

clue.text: Disappointing projection when demand is low

parts.note: something off is poor or disappointing
a peak is a projecting point, such as a cap's brim

explanation.surface: A letdown of a forecast about falling sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak hours are times of lower demand, when fares and tariffs are cheaper.

clue.text: Censure Damian, vile type

indicators.note: vile suggests something corrupted, so these letters are distorted

parts.note: a version is a type or variant

explanation.surface: Someone condemns Damian as a nasty sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vile' rearranges DAMIAN into ANIMAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Animadversion is a formal word for criticism or condemnation.
